title: openai-compat: align tool calling schema mapping and tool_choice semantics; tool message formatting fixes
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Improve Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling to match recent upstream semantics around tool_choice, ensure correct mapping between Redwood tool schemas and OpenAI-compatible JSON schemas, and fix inconsistencies in how tool-generated messages are formatted and streamed. This addresses user-reported edge cases where the model emits tool_choice with ambiguous args, and where SDKs received malformed tool messages during streaming.

What this PR does: 
- Implements a schema-mapping layer that converts Redwood tool definitions (typed argument specs, optional/required fields, nested objects) into an OpenAI-compatible JSON schema payload for model tool calling. The mapper preserves type coercion rules, nullable semantics, and provides warnings for mismatches.
- Adds robust handling for tool_choice semantics: when the model returns a tool_choice selection the runtime validates the selected tool name against the current tool set, resolves aliases, and performs argument validation and normalization prior to invoking the tool. If validation fails, runtime emits a clear assistant message and falls back to the previous model response path.
- Normalizes tool message formatting: tool outputs are now wrapped consistently as tool messages with the expected metadata fields (tool_name, content_type, content) and a short sanitization pass to strip invalid control chars. Streaming logic was updated to stream tool messages as tool-role chunks so clients using OpenAI-compatible streaming see the same event sequence as upstream.
- Adds a feature flag OPENAI_COMP_TOOL_CHOICE (default: true) to gate some of the more aggressive fallback behaviors for customers who depend on previous permissive behavior.

Checklist: 
- [x] Schema mapper implementation and unit tests 
- [x] tool_choice resolver and validation logic 
- [x] Streaming updates for tool messages and SDKs 
- [x] Docs: updated OpenAI-compat function-calling doc and migration notes 
- [x] E2E integration tests in redwood/tests covering cross-repo SDK behavior 
- [x] Canary rollout plan and feature flag gating

Testing and validation: 
- Added unit tests exercising nested schema mapping, missing/extra fields, and coercion rules.
- Updated integration tests to run end-to-end through the runtime -> tool shim and back to SDKs.
- Ran perf canary on dedicated capacity; no observable token-latency regressions beyond noise (bench results in CI output).
- Verified streaming event order against OpenAI reference (tool role events appear as expected).

Compatibility notes: 
- Backwards compatible by default (OPENAI_COMP_TOOL_CHOICE off) for customers that depend on older permissive behavior. When enabled, the stricter validation may surface argument validation errors which are surfaced as assistant messages; we document the migration steps in redwood-docs.

Rollout plan: 
- Merge to main behind feature flag.
- Canary enable for 5% of traffic on Redwood-hosted API for one week.
- Monitor errors, tool invocation failures, and SDK regressions via dashboards added in this PR.
- Gradually increase to 100% if no regressions are observed.

Related: Linear ENG-4521, ENG-4620. SUP ticket SUP-1129 attached for customer-reported issue in production.
